reviewed_by: Claude (early-fragment-token bug loop); selection reviewed against the diff by the implementing agent, root cause independently validated by a separate subagent
reason: The browser read a launcher #token= fragment only inside WorkspaceProvider's effect; routes that redirect on first render (/sessions, /agents, /missions, /work, the * catch-all) ran their child Navigate effect first and replaced the URL without the fragment, so such links opened 'Browser session expired'. runtime.ts exports captureBrowserFragmentToken() and main.tsx calls it before rendering (skipped for Tauri and Electron). Frontend: runtime.test (new regression: a startup-captured token survives a redirect that drops the fragment, plus the existing fragment-consumption tests).
exclusions: No Python, native or Playwright selection: no Core change, and no mocked Playwright spec opens a legacy route with #token= (playwright_impact select returned no areas). Revalidated on the staging Core with the production bundle in Chromium and WebKit: /sessions, /agents, /missions, /work, an unknown path and / opened with #token= are all authorized and the token never remains in the URL.
